summary: Modern databases have rapidly evolved to embed AI and ML capabilities natively, eliminating the need to move data to external systems for inference, vector search, and LLM-powered analytics. By 2026, vector search support has become a standard expectation across both purpose-built and general-purpose databases, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities. Platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and PostgreSQL now offer deep LLM integration, managed embeddings, and semantic search directly within the data layer, reducing infrastructure complexity and governance risk.

databases.name: Snowflake
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of fully managed LLM and ML functions running natively inside the AI Data Cloud. It includes COMPLETE() for text generation, SUMMARIZE(), SENTIMENT(), TRANSLATE(), and EMBED_TEXT() for generating vector embeddings. Cortex Analyst enables natural language querying of structured data, while Cortex Search powers semantic and hybrid search over unstructured content. Snowflake Postgres (generally available in 2026) runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates with Cortex for AI functions, with pgvector support enabling vector similarity search without additional infrastructure. Data never leaves the Snowflake security perimeter during inference.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM inference via Cortex AI supporting models including Mistral, LLaMA, Mixtral, and Arctic (Snowflake's own LLM). Cortex integrates with Snowflake Postgres and pgvector for embedding storage and similarity search. External model access via Cortex External Functions connects to third-party providers like OpenAI and Anthropic.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. LLM inference costs vary by model; for example, COMPLETE() with Mistral-7B costs roughly 0.015 credits per 1K tokens. Embedding generation via EMBED_TEXT() is charged per token. Snowflake Postgres is priced separately as a managed Postgres offering within the AI Data Cloud. Overall costs scale with compute and token usage, with no separate per-seat charge for Cortex access.

databases.name: Google BigQuery
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to create and execute ML models using standard SQL directly inside BigQuery, supporting logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, boosted trees, AutoML, and deep neural networks. BigQuery Vector Search extends this with native approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over embedding columns stored in BigQuery tables. Through Vertex AI integration, users can call remotely hosted foundation models such as Gemini directly from SQL using ML.GENERATE_TEXT() and ML.EMBED_TEXT() functions, enabling RAG pipelines and semantic search without data movement. BigQuery Omni extends these capabilities to data stored in AWS S3 or Azure Blob.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Google Vertex AI and Gemini model family via remote model connections. ML.GENERATE_TEXT() and ML.UNDERSTAND_TEXT() allow LLM inference in SQL. ML.EMBED_TEXT() generates embeddings using Vertex AI text-embedding models. Supports external model endpoints for OpenAI-compatible APIs via Vertex AI Model Garden.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference is billed per byte processed (on-demand) or covered under flat-rate capacity slots. Vector Search queries are charged per byte scanned. LLM inference calls via ML.GENERATE_TEXT() pass through Vertex AI pricing, typically $0.00025–$0.001 per 1K characters depending on the Gemini model tier. Embedding generation via Vertex AI is billed separately at approximately $0.0001 per 1K characters for text-embedding-004.

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector similarity search, supporting exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW and IVFFlat indexing methods. It stores embeddings as native vector columns and supports L2 distance, cosine similarity, and inner product operators. pgai (from Timescale) complements pgvector by adding SQL functions to call external LLM APIs such as OpenAI, Ollama, and Anthropic directly from PostgreSQL, enabling embedding generation, text completion, and reranking without leaving the database. Together they make PostgreSQL a fully capable RAG backend, handling up to approximately 50 million vectors comfortably according to 2026 production benchmarks. Snowflake Postgres and Supabase also ship pgvector as a managed offering.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension provides direct SQL-level access to OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and Cohere APIs for embedding generation and LLM completion. Vectorizer feature in pgai (Timescale Cloud) automates embedding creation and synchronization. Works natively within Snowflake Postgres with Cortex AI functions and within Supabase for managed deployments.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to self-host on any PostgreSQL instance. Managed offerings vary: Supabase Vector includes pgvector on free and Pro plans (Pro from $25/month). Timescale Cloud includes pgai and automated vectorizers on paid plans starting around $95/month for production workloads. Snowflake Postgres is billed within Snowflake credits. LLM API calls via pgai are billed by the respective provider (e.g., OpenAI API rates apply separately).

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL databases to invoke Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock models directly via SQL functions, allowing classification, regression, and generative AI inference without data leaving the VPC. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector for native vector similarity search, making it a managed vector-capable relational database. Amazon Redshift ML allows data warehouse users to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL by connecting to SageMaker AutoPilot, and supports calling Bedrock foundation models for text generation and embedding tasks directly from Redshift queries. Amazon Bedrock integration across both services provides access to models from Anthropic Claude, Meta LLaMA, Amazon Titan, Cohere, and others.
databases.llm_integration: Integration with Amazon Bedrock provides access to Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan Text and Titan Embeddings, Meta LLaMA, Cohere Command, and Mistral models via SQL. Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector for embedding storage and ANN search. Redshift ML connects to SageMaker for custom model training and Bedrock for foundation model inference. IAM-based access control governs all cross-service calls.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference charges are based on SageMaker or Bedrock API call costs passed through, plus standard Aurora instance pricing. Redshift ML model training incurs SageMaker training instance costs; inference calls to Bedrock are billed per token at Bedrock rates (e.g., Claude 3 Haiku at approximately $0.00025 per 1K input tokens). pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional licensing cost beyond standard Aurora instance pricing. Bedrock costs vary widely by model and are billed separately from database compute.

databases.name: Databricks
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI and ML platform built on Apache Spark with MLflow as the open-source backbone for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source LLM, available for fine-tuning and inference within the Lakehouse. Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks ML) encompasses Vector Search for storing and querying embeddings natively in Delta Lake tables, Model Serving for real-time inference endpoints, AI Playground for prompt engineering, and Agent Framework for building and evaluating LLM-based agents. Databricks Vector Search supports DELTA_SYNC indexes that automatically stay in sync with source Delta tables and handles both similarity search and hybrid keyword-vector search. The platform integrates with pgvector environments and Snowflake via data mirroring for analytics pipelines.
databases.llm_integration: Supports DBRX, LLaMA 3, Mixtral, and other open models via Mosaic AI Model Serving. External model integration supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Azure OpenAI via the AI Gateway with unified rate limiting and logging. MLflow tracks all model versions and experiments. Foundation Model APIs provide pay-per-token access to curated models including Meta LLaMA 3.1 and DBRX Instruct without managing infrastructure.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks billing is based on Databricks Units (DBUs). Vector Search indexes incur DBU costs for ingestion and query compute. Model Serving endpoints are billed per DBU-hour for provisioned throughput or per token for Foundation Model APIs (LLaMA 3.1 70B approximately $0.001 per 1K tokens). MLflow OSS is free; managed MLflow on Databricks is included in workspace costs. Premium and Enterprise plans required for full Mosaic AI feature access. Costs vary significantly by cloud provider and region.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is a fully managed vector search capability built natively into Atlas, supporting approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW indexing over vector embeddings stored alongside operational document data. It supports filtering by metadata fields, enabling pre-filtered semantic search without post-processing. Atlas Vector Search integrates with major AI frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack, and works with embedding providers such as OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, and Google Vertex AI. Atlas Search Nodes (dedicated infrastructure for search and vector workloads) allow independent scaling of vector search from database compute. MongoDB also offers Atlas Stream Processing and a Triggers-based vectorizer to automate embedding generation on document insert or update.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack for RAG pipeline construction. Embedding generation supported via connections to OpenAI text-embedding models, Cohere Embed, Google Vertex AI, and Hugging Face inference endpoints. Atlas Functions and Triggers can call external LLM APIs automatically on data changes. No proprietary LLM is embedded; Atlas serves as the vector store and document retrieval layer within third-party LLM stacks.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above (starting approximately $57/month for M10 on AWS). Atlas Search Nodes for dedicated vector search infrastructure start at approximately $0.08/hour per node. Vector index storage is included in cluster storage pricing. There are no separate per-query charges for vector search; costs scale with cluster tier and storage. Free tier (M0) does not support Vector Search indexes.
